preamble: Glide formation turns the mid back vowel [o] into the labio-velar glide [w] when it stands before another vowel, resolving hiatus. The vowel raises to [+high] and becomes non-syllabic, so the sequence becomes a rising diphthong. It happened historically in Western Romance (Latin coāgulāre > Spanish cuajar) and is productive in colloquial Spanish across word boundaries. Comparative surveys of hiatus resolution also report o-gliding (o+a > wa) in Bantu languages such as isiXhosa.

examples.note: In casual speech, word-final mid /o/ glides to [w] before a following vowel that differs from it in backness or height.

examples.from: tengo hipo /tengo # ipo/ 'I have the hiccups'

examples.note: The Latin hiatus o.a became the rising diphthong [wa] through Old Spanish quajar. The learned doublet coagular keeps the hiatus.

sources: Baković, E. (2006). Hiatus resolution and incomplete identity. Rutgers Optimality Archive ROA-813. https://roa.rutgers.edu/files/813-0306/813-BAKOVIC-0-0.PDF
Fang, C.-S. (2019). Hiatus resolution in Formosan Austronesian and selected Bantu languages: a comparative analysis. MA thesis, University of the Witwatersrand. https://hdl.handle.net/10539/29458
